newsitem.title: UK: Guinness, GrandMet open door to proposals.
newsitem.headline: Guinness, GrandMet open door to proposals.

text.p: Drinks group Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc said on Wednesday they were open to proposals from Bernard Arnault, chairman of LVMH Moet Hennessey Louis Vuitton, who is opposing a merger of the two groups.

"We have made it clear to Mr Arnault that we are, of course, open to any proposals provided that they create additional value for our shareholders beyond our existing proposal and that this is fairly shared between them," said GrandMet and Guinness in a joint statement.
"Accordingly, at our meeting today, we asked Mr Arnault to detail in writing his specific proposals so that we can evaluate them against these critiria. He has agreed to do this," said the statement.
The statement followed a meeting, held at LVMH's head office in Paris, between Guinness chairman Tony Greener, GrandMet chairman George Bull and Arnault.

It was the first meeting held with Arnault, who is a Guinness board member and its largest shareholder with a 14.2 percent stake, since Guinness and GrandMet announced their planned 24 billion pound ($39.8 billion) merger on May 12.
Since then Arnault has spent more than eight billion francs ($1.4 billion) to build up a 6.4 percent holding in Grand Met in an apparent attempt to block the merger outright.
A 10 percent stake would allow him to call an extraordinary meeting of GrandMet shareholders and try to win enough of them over to his argument.

Arnault wants to involve his Moet Hennessy drinks division in a three way tie up in spirits. Some analysts speculate this may be achieved by selling it to GMG Brands, the name given to the merged GrandMet/Guinness group, for a price estimated at between 2.0 billion and 2.4 billion pounds.

British newspapers have also said Guinness and GrandMet may propose to include Moet Hennessy in UDV, the new company formed by the merger of United Distillers and IDV, the spirits divisions of Guinness and GrandMet respectively. In turn, LVMH would take a stake in UDV estimated at 30 to 35 percent.

Arnault has also initiated legal action, seeking the right to exercise options to buy Guinness out of their valuable joint distribution ventures after the British partners refused to consider his plan.
